source_title: 5 best anime series based on the popular video games - The Times of India
source_excerpt: A great video game can keep players hooked for hundreds of hours, but bringing that same magic to an anime screen is a different challenge. Some adaptations struggle to capture what made their original games special, while others find new ways to make familiar characters and stories stand out. From supernatural battles and courtroom mysteries to high-speed adventures and emotional fantasy journeys, several anime have built their own appeal beyond the gaming world. These five video game adaptations offer something worth exploring, whether you already know the games or are looking for your next anime to watch.1. Persona 5: The Animation The Phantom Thieves of Hearts made a strong impression in the gaming world with their stylish adventures, secret identities and fight against corruption. Persona 5: The Animation brings that story to television, following Ren Amamiya and his friends as they discover the Metaverse, a strange realm where distorted desires take physical form.The series follows the group's efforts to change the hearts of people who abuse their power. Its supernatural setting gives the story plenty of action, but the friendships between the characters remain central to the experience. Fans of the game will recognise familiar moments, locations and characters, while newcomers can discover a world where ordinary students lead extraordinary double lives.2. Sonic X Sonic the Hedgehog is known for speed, colourful worlds and a never-ending rivalry with Dr. Eggman. Sonic X takes those familiar ingredients and sends Sonic and his friends into an unfamiliar setting when a mishap involving Chaos Control transports them to Earth.There, Sonic meets Chris Thorndyke, a human boy who becomes involved in the hedgehog's efforts to collect the Chaos Emeralds and find a way home. The story combines fast-paced adventures with quieter moments that explore the relationships between Sonic, his friends and their human companions.3. Ace Attorney Courtroom drama might seem like an unusual starting point for an anime, but Ace Attorney makes it work through clever mysteries, dramatic confrontations and unexpected discoveries. The series follows rookie defence attorney Phoenix Wright as he takes on cases that often appear impossible to solve.With help from Maya Fey and other allies, Phoenix investigates suspicious incidents, questions witnesses and searches for contradictions that could reveal the truth. Each case challenges him to look beyond the obvious, turning courtroom arguments into tense battles of logic.4. Tales Of The Abyss Tales of the Abyss follows Luke fon Fabre, a privileged young man whose sheltered life changes after an unexpected encounter sends him into a much larger conflict. As he travels beyond the world he knows, he begins to question his identity, his responsibilities and the beliefs that have shaped his life.Based on the role-playing game from the Tales franchise, the anime combines fantasy adventure with political tensions, ancient prophecies and questions about personal choice. Luke's development gives the story its emotional centre. His journey is not simply about defeating enemies but also about understanding the consequences of his actions.5. Brotherhood: Final Fantasy XV Before players follow Noctis on his journey in Final Fantasy XV, Brotherhood: Final Fantasy XV offers a closer look at the relationships that shape him and his closest friends. The animated series focuses on Noctis, Gladiolus, Ignis and Prompto, exploring parts of their lives and experiences that help explain their bond.Rather than retelling the entire game, the series adds context to the characters and their shared history. Each episode offers a glimpse into their personalities, fears and motivations, helping viewers understand why their friendship matters when the larger adventure begins.For existing fans, the anime provides extra insight into the four central characters.
